newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. stock index futures end lower.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. stock index futures end lower.

text.p: Most U.S. stock index futures closed lower on a technical sell-off that switched the direction of Standard & Poor's 500s contracts at mid-morning, traders and analysts said.
"When you gap up the way S&Ps did at the opening, something has to give a little," one S&P futures trader said.
"What more do you want," another trader said. "We were up quite a bit on Monday."
December S&Ps were bombarded with heavy selling pressure from several large commission houses and from locals who pushed the market in both directions and lifted S&Ps off their lows.
"Locals were racing each other with absolutely no volume," one floor source said about the lackluster activity late in the day.
While analysts said the daily sentiment was positive, and confidence was building at these higher levels, most said they were looking for December to trade in a sideways range in the near term.
"We have a lot of work to do in the low 700 level," an analyst said. "We could even re-visit the area below 700."
He said good third-quarter earnings from technology companies led to overextended gains.

On GLOBEX, December S&Ps shot to 712.40, just shy of a 5.00-point extension from Tuesday's settlement price of 707.50. At the start of pit trade, December immediately rose to the 5.00-point opening limit and traded at a contract high of 712.50 for 10 minutes.
A two-minute trading halt was imposed at 0840 CDT/1340 GMT.

When the market re-opened, the contract was already hit by offers in the pit and arbitrage buy programs, which occurred later as December traded about 3.90 points above cash S&Ps. Fair value is at 4.50 points.
Arbitrage buy programs were at a premium of 5.45 points to cash, traders said.
They said selling gained momentum when December fell through its previous contract high at 710.60, and propelled the contract to the intraday low of 702.80.
December broke through Monday's session low of 705.40 and the 22-month weekly bullish trendline at 704.40.
They also said the renewed strength in the U.S. dollar raised the enthusiasm a notch too high in the U.S. stock market.
The U.S. dollar's surge kept Nikkei futures sharply higher throughout the day. December rose to an intraday high of 21,900, and closed up 460 points at 21,630.

At the end of pit trade, December S&Ps were off 0.85 at 706.65, New Composites were down 0.60 at 375.35, KBT Value Lines were down 1.35 at 650.55, Nasdaq 100s were up 1.35 at 781.20 and Midcaps were off 0.40 at 247.05. -Derivative desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com
